easy.explanation: He asked them to send him away to his master.

easy.question: Who asked Rebekah to stay a few days, at least ten?
easy.explanation: Her brother and mother asked her to remain longer.

easy.question: What did Rebekah answer when asked whether she would go?
easy.explanation: Rebekah answered clearly, “I will go.”

medium.question: What happened after the group ate and drank?
answers: They stayed overnight, and the man asked to leave in the morning
They asked Rebekah to stay ten days
medium.explanation: They spent the night, then the servant asked to depart in the morning.

medium.question: Why did the man ask them not to delay him?
answers: He did not want to eat
The Lord had prospered his way, and he wanted to return to his master
medium.explanation: He believed God had made the journey successful and wanted to continue.

medium.question: What does “at least ten” mean?
medium.explanation: The family requested that Rebekah stay for ten days.

challenge.question: Why did the family ask Rebekah herself before sending her?
answers: To let her express her own choice
To see whether she knew the way
challenge.explanation: They asked Rebekah directly and allowed her to decide.

challenge.question: What does the disagreement reveal?
answers: The family wanted delay, while the servant wanted to leave
The servant did not want Rebekah to go
challenge.explanation: The family requested more time, but the servant wanted to depart promptly.

challenge.question: What is notable about Rebekah’s answer?
answers: She asked to wait until morning
She agreed only if her mother came
She gave a brief and definite consent
challenge.explanation: Despite the request for delay, Rebekah clearly agreed to go.

answers: To let her express her own choice
To see whether she knew the way
questions.explanation: They asked Rebekah directly and allowed her to decide.

answers: The family wanted delay, while the servant wanted to leave
The servant did not want Rebekah to go

paragraphs.title: The Family’s Blessing and Rebekah’s Departure

easy.question: Who sent Rebekah away?
easy.explanation: Her family sent her on her journey.

easy.question: Who went with Rebekah?
answers: Her nurse, Abraham’s servant, and his men
easy.explanation: The passage lists her nurse, the servant, and his men.

easy.question: What did her family wish for her?
answers: That she become very fruitful and that her descendants defeat their enemies
easy.explanation: They blessed her with many descendants and victory over her enemies.

medium.question: What happened after the family sent Rebekah?
medium.explanation: The blessing followed her departure.

medium.question: What was Rebekah’s nurse?
answers: A woman who had nursed and raised her
medium.explanation: The nurse was a woman who cared for Rebekah as she grew up.

medium.question: How do the two parts of the blessing fit together?
answers: They promise that she will return
They wish her many descendants and victory over enemies
medium.explanation: The blessing includes both abundant offspring and triumph over enemies.

challenge.question: What does “mother of thousands of millions” express?
answers: She would own a thousand houses
She and her descendants would become very numerous
She would travel ten thousand days
challenge.explanation: It is a blessing for an exceedingly large number of descendants.

challenge.question: What does possessing the gate of enemies mean?
challenge.explanation: The city gate represented power and authority; possessing it signifies victory.

challenge.question: Who likely spoke the blessing beginning “Our sister”?
challenge.explanation: Those who called her “our sister” were her family members.

questions.question: What does “mother of thousands of millions” express?
answers: She would own a thousand houses
She and her descendants would become very numerous
She would travel ten thousand days
questions.explanation: It is a blessing for an exceedingly large number of descendants.

questions.question: What does possessing the gate of enemies mean?
questions.explanation: The city gate represented power and authority; possessing it signifies victory.

questions.question: Who likely spoke the blessing beginning “Our sister”?
questions.explanation: Those who called her “our sister” were her family members.

easy.question: Who rose with her attendants?
easy.explanation: Rebekah and her attendants rose to leave.

easy.question: What did Rebekah ride?
easy.explanation: Rebekah and her attendants rode the camels.

easy.question: Who took Rebekah and departed?
easy.explanation: The servant took Rebekah and went on his way.

medium.question: What did Rebekah and her attendants do after rising?
medium.explanation: They mounted the camels and followed the man.

medium.question: What does “followed the man” mean?
medium.explanation: The women went after or behind the servant.

medium.question: What was the sequence of events?
answers: Rebekah rose, rode a camel, and followed the man
She followed the man, then rose and rode
The servant left, then Rebekah rose at home
medium.explanation: The verse presents those actions in that order.

challenge.question: What does the plural “they rode” show?
answers: The servant and his men rode
challenge.explanation: The plural refers to Rebekah and her attendants.

challenge.question: What does “followed the man” imply about the journey?
answers: The man waited at the well
challenge.explanation: The group traveled after the servant, who led the way.

challenge.question: What shows that Rebekah traveled with other women?
challenge.explanation: “Her attendants” shows that she did not travel alone.

questions.question: What does the plural “they rode” show?
answers: The servant and his men rode
questions.explanation: The plural refers to Rebekah and her attendants.

questions.question: What does “followed the man” imply about the journey?
answers: The man waited at the well
questions.explanation: The group traveled after the servant, who led the way.

questions.question: What shows that Rebekah traveled with other women?
questions.explanation: “Her attendants” shows that she did not travel alone.

paragraphs.title: Isaac in the Field and the Camels

easy.question: Where did Isaac live?
easy.explanation: Isaac lived in the south country.

easy.question: What did Isaac do toward evening?
answers: Went out to meditate in the field
easy.explanation: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at evening.

easy.question: What did Isaac see when he lifted his eyes?
easy.explanation: He saw camels approaching.

medium.question: What was the order of events?
answers: Isaac went to the field, lifted his eyes, and saw camels
He saw camels, went to the field, and lifted his eyes
He returned home and then saw camels
medium.explanation: The verse gives that sequence.

medium.question: What does “at the eventide” mean?
medium.explanation: It means near the end of the day.

medium.question: What places are mentioned?
answers: Isaac lived in Lahairoi and came from the south
He lived in Egypt and came from Lahairoi
He came from Lahairoi and lived in the south
medium.explanation: The verse distinguishes Lahairoi, where he came from, from the southern country where he lived.

challenge.question: What does “behold” emphasize in “the camels were coming”?
answers: The camels appeared suddenly or notably
The camels had stood there for a long time
challenge.explanation: “Behold” draws attention to the camels’ unexpected appearance.

challenge.question: Who lifted his eyes and saw the camels?
challenge.explanation: The verse describes Isaac lifting his eyes and seeing them.

challenge.question: What is the important distinction between the places mentioned?
answers: Lahairoi was where Isaac lived and the south was where he came from
They were exactly the same place
Isaac came from Lahairoi and lived in the south
challenge.explanation: The verse says Isaac came from Lahairoi but lived in the southern country.

questions.question: What does “behold” emphasize in “the camels were coming”?
answers: The camels appeared suddenly or notably
The camels had stood there for a long time
questions.explanation: “Behold” draws attention to the camels’ unexpected appearance.

questions.question: Who lifted his eyes and saw the camels?
questions.explanation: The verse describes Isaac lifting his eyes and seeing them.

questions.question: What is the important distinction between the places mentioned?
answers: Lahairoi was where Isaac lived and the south was where he came from
They were exactly the same place
Isaac came from Lahairoi and lived in the south
questions.explanation: The verse says Isaac came from Lahairoi but lived in the southern country.

easy.question: Who saw Isaac?
easy.explanation: Rebekah lifted her eyes and saw Isaac.

easy.question: From what animal did Rebekah get down?
easy.explanation: She got down from the camel.

easy.question: What did Rebekah do after learning that the man was Isaac?
answers: Took a veil and covered herself
easy.explanation: She took a veil and covered herself.

medium.question: What was the correct sequence?
answers: Rebekah covered herself, saw Isaac, and asked who he was
She saw Isaac, asked the servant who he was, and then covered herself
The servant identified Isaac, Rebekah saw him, and then she dismounted
medium.explanation: Rebekah saw Isaac, asked about him, and then covered herself.

medium.question: In “What man is this,” what does “this” refer to?
medium.explanation: Rebekah was pointing to the man approaching them.

medium.question: Why did Rebekah ask who the man was?
answers: She wanted to know where the field was
She did not know the identity of the approaching man
medium.explanation: She saw Isaac but did not yet know who he was.

challenge.question: What may Rebekah’s veil indicate?
answers: Modesty and respect before meeting Isaac
challenge.explanation: She covered herself upon learning that she was approaching Isaac.

challenge.question: What does “walking in the field to meet us” show about Isaac?
answers: He was approaching Rebekah and the servant
challenge.explanation: “To meet us” indicates movement toward them.

challenge.question: Who did the servant mean by “my master”?
challenge.explanation: The man Rebekah asked about was Isaac, the servant’s master.

questions.question: What may Rebekah’s veil indicate?
answers: Modesty and respect before meeting Isaac
questions.explanation: She covered herself upon learning that she was approaching Isaac.

questions.question: What does “walking in the field to meet us” show about Isaac?
answers: He was approaching Rebekah and the servant
questions.explanation: “To meet us” indicates movement toward them.

questions.question: Who did the servant mean by “my master”?
questions.explanation: The man Rebekah asked about was Isaac, the servant’s master.

easy.question: To whom did the servant tell everything he had done?
easy.explanation: The servant told Isaac the whole story.

easy.question: Whom did Isaac bring into his mother Sarah’s tent?
easy.explanation: Isaac brought Rebekah into Sarah’s tent.

easy.question: What did Rebekah become to Isaac?
easy.explanation: Rebekah became Isaac’s wife.

medium.question: What did Isaac do after hearing the servant’s story?
answers: He took Rebekah as his wife
medium.explanation: Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother’s tent and married her.

medium.question: What does “Isaac was comforted” mean?
medium.explanation: Isaac found comfort after his mother’s death.

medium.question: What is the sequence in the verses?
answers: Isaac loved Rebekah, then the servant spoke
Rebekah became his wife, then Isaac brought her
The servant told Isaac, Isaac brought Rebekah, and she became his wife
medium.explanation: The passage presents the servant’s report, Isaac’s welcome, and the marriage.

challenge.question: Why is Sarah’s tent mentioned?
answers: Rebekah entered a place closely connected with Isaac’s family
challenge.explanation: Bringing Rebekah into Sarah’s tent emphasizes her entrance into Isaac’s family.

challenge.question: What does “he loved her” emphasize?
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly states Isaac’s love for Rebekah.

challenge.question: How are Isaac’s love and comfort connected?
answers: He mourned Rebekah instead of Sarah
Rebekah told him the servant’s story
His relationship with Rebekah comforted him after losing his mother
challenge.explanation: The verse connects his love for Rebekah with his comfort after Sarah’s death.

answers: Rebekah entered a place closely connected with Isaac’s family
questions.explanation: Bringing Rebekah into Sarah’s tent emphasizes her entrance into Isaac’s family.

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states Isaac’s love for Rebekah.
